name: Airbus A319/A320/A321 (ceo)
summary: The original A320 family of 6-abreast single-aisle jets, the backbone of American, Delta, United, JetBlue, Allegiant and others.

wings: Low swept wing with small arrowhead wingtip fences above and below the tip on older airframes
Later builds and retrofits carry tall curved sharklets instead
Wing root with a prominent fairing and short main gear legs
engines: Two underwing turbofans of moderate diameter: short round CFM56 nacelles or long full-length IAE V2500 nacelles
Nacelle bottoms sit well clear of the ground and close under the wing
fuselage: Circular 6-abreast fuselage; A319 short, A320 medium, A321 long with extra doors ahead of and behind the wing
Rounded, blunt nose with a six-pane windshield whose lower edge runs in a straight line
Main wheels retract into covered wells — in flight the belly looks smooth
tail: Tall swept fin with a pointed tip and a small dorsal fillet
Tailcone ends in a horizontal wedge with the APU exhaust

tellTales: Small arrowhead fences at the wingtips (if fitted)
Blunt rounded nose with straight-bottomed cockpit windows
Moderate-size engines that do not reach far ahead of the wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The ceo has noticeably smaller nacelles that hang well clear of the ground; the neo's much fatter LEAP or GTF nacelles reach far ahead of the wing, and wingtip fences mean it is definitely a ceo.
The A320 has a rounded blunt nose, taller gear and covered main wheels; the 737NG has a pointed nose, V-shaped cockpit side windows, flat-bottomed engine intakes and exposed wheel hubs.
The A320 is wider (6-abreast) with smaller engines relative to its body and wingtip fences or sharklets; the A220 has plain wingtips and oversized engines.
The A321 is shorter-legged with a rounded Airbus nose and smaller engines; the 757 stands on tall gear with a droopy pointed nose and very large engines.

usCount.source: Airline fleet data (American, Delta, United, JetBlue, Allegiant, Spirit; planespotters.net / ch-aviation)
